Silver rules backtest, 26 years: 20 Nov 2000 to 20 Nov 2026 (US Eastern time)

Every silver rule in the project (TA Section 35 and other TA/KD silver items, the 2026 document's silver section; your Sun notes are gold-only and are not used). Failure analysis reads the Moon, silver's classical significator (TA p.32; Kindle Ch15), and checks whether gold made the same move, recomputed with the Swiss-Ephemeris engine (Lahiri, mean node, whole-sign drishti) and scored against COMEX silver futures daily closes (Yahoo Finance SI=F continuous front month). Silver went from 4.6 (17 Nov 2000) to 41.0 (20 Nov 2026), +783.4%, peaking at 115.1 on 26 Jan 2026 (largest one-day fall -31.3%).

Rules that fired55

Key findings

  1. Overall. 1083 of 2133 decided occurrences worked (51%), against 51% expected by chance from the base rates of those same occurrences (p = 0.560 for doing this well or better by luck). On the 646 trading days when more bearish than bullish silver rules were active, silver moved +0.23% on average over the next 5 days (54% up); on the 4946 bullish-majority days, +0.22% (53% up). Correlation of the daily net count with the next 5-day move: -0.024.
  2. Statistically clear results (p < 0.05 against the base rate):
    • None of the rules beat chance at that level.
    • Significantly wrong: Mars rising (after combustion) (Bullish): 2 of 10 worked (20% vs base 54%), average move -3.43% in the stated direction; p = 0.995; right in 2 of 10 years with a result
  3. What worked (most decided occurrences first):
    • Mars Vargottam in Cancer (Bearish): 8 of 14 worked (57% vs base 45%), average move +0.36% in the stated direction; p = 0.254; right in 8 of 14 years with a result
    • Moon is Mantri of the year (Bearish): 4 of 6 worked (67% vs base 50%), average move +1.29% in the stated direction; p = 0.349; right in 4 of 6 years with a result
    • Rahu does Vedha of Pushya (Bullish): 3 of 4 worked (75% vs base 47%), average move +5.54% in the stated direction; p = 0.271; right in 3 of 4 years with a result
    • Rahu in Dhanishta (market and bullion risk) (Bearish): 2 of 2 worked (100% vs base 69%), average move +19.43% in the stated direction; p = 0.470; right in 2 of 2 years with a result
    • Jupiter enters Scorpio (Bullish): 2 of 2 worked (100% vs base 54%), average move +2.11% in the stated direction; p = 0.296; right in 2 of 2 years with a result
    • Saturn-Neptune conjunction (Bullish): 1 of 1 worked (100% vs base 48%), average move +12.16% in the stated direction; p = 0.481; right in 1 of 1 years with a result
  4. What failed:
    • Mercury alone in Aries or Virgo (Bearish): 11 of 33 worked (33% vs base 45%), average move -0.68% in the stated direction; p = 0.940; right in 7 of 22 years with a result
    • Saturn direct from retrograde (Bearish): 8 of 23 worked (35% vs base 46%), average move -1.49% in the stated direction; p = 0.898; right in 8 of 23 years with a result
    • Jupiter turns direct from retrograde (Bullish): 9 of 21 worked (43% vs base 54%), average move -1.01% in the stated direction; p = 0.899; right in 9 of 21 years with a result
    • Mercury does Vedha of Venus (Bullish): 8 of 18 worked (44% vs base 54%), average move -0.18% in the stated direction; p = 0.858; right in 6 of 15 years with a result
    • Venus combust in West (Bullish): 5 of 13 worked (38% vs base 54%), average move -1.32% in the stated direction; p = 0.923; right in 5 of 13 years with a result
    • Moon eclipse on Sunday (Bearish): 2 of 11 worked (18% vs base 45%), average move -1.87% in the stated direction; p = 0.986; right in 1 of 9 years with a result
    • Mars rising (after combustion) (Bullish): 2 of 10 worked (20% vs base 54%), average move -3.43% in the stated direction; p = 0.995; right in 2 of 10 years with a result
    • Mars in Gemini with any 2 other planets (Bearish): 1 of 7 worked (14% vs base 48%), average move -1.59% in the stated direction; p = 0.989; right in 1 of 6 years with a result
    • Cancer Sankranti on Saturday (Bearish): 1 of 3 worked (33% vs base 45%), average move -0.61% in the stated direction; p = 0.833; right in 1 of 3 years with a result
    • Retrograde Mars entering Taurus or Libra (Bullish): 0 of 2 worked (0% vs base 50%), average move -2.25% in the stated direction; p = 1.000; right in 0 of 2 years with a result
    • Rahu enters Gemini (Bearish): 0 of 1 worked (0% vs base 44%), average move -2.52% in the stated direction; p = 1.000; right in 0 of 1 years with a result
  5. Why bullish rules failed. Conditions clearly more common when they failed: Gold moved against the rule too (>0.5%) (73% of failures vs 8% of successes). More common when they worked: none stood out.
  6. Why bearish rules failed. Conditions clearly more common when they failed: Gold moved against the rule too (>0.5%) (79% of failures vs 13% of successes); Saturn / Rahu / Ketu on the Moon at the start (52% of failures vs 39% of successes). More common when they worked: none stood out.
  7. Silver follows gold. Over the same dates silver moved the same way as gold in 1610 of 2130 decided occurrences (76%). When gold moved against a silver rule the rule failed 793 of 900 times (88%); when gold moved the rule's way it worked 817 of 935 times (87%). So a silver rule's outcome was decided mostly by gold's direction: the rules add little that is specific to silver.
  8. Biggest single miss: late January 2026 (2026-01-26 → 2026-02-02, -33.3%, including the −31% day on 30 Jan, the same day gold fell 10.8%). Silver rules active: 3 bullish, 1 bearish. Sky: Sun in Shravana (lord Moon), Capricorn; Mercury with Sun, Venus with Sun, Mars with Sun; Jupiter Gemini Punarvasu R; 29 Jan: Mercury conjunction Venus in Capricorn; 31 Jan-01 Feb: Venus combust.
  9. The 15 biggest 5-day falls: bearish rules outnumbered bullish ones in 1 of them; in the rest the rule set leaned bullish going into the fall (it leans bullish on 76% of all trading days, so a bullish majority by itself carries little information). 2026-01-26 -33.3% (3:1); 2020-03-11 -29.9% (3:0); 2011-04-29 -27.4% (3:2); 2011-09-16 -26.3% (6:2); 2008-10-09 -18.7% (7:4); 2006-06-06 -18.7% (2:0); 2008-09-04 -18.4% (7:2); 2026-06-17 -17.5% (3:0).
  10. The 15 biggest 5-day rises: bullish rules outnumbered bearish ones in 12 of them.
  11. How far to trust this. 26 years give the frequent rules (vedha, Mercury/Sun contacts, paksha length, retrogrades) enough occurrences to judge; 11 rules still have fewer than 5 decided occurrences, and their records stay anecdotal. A rule that is right in most individual years is more trustworthy than one whose total comes from a single year; check the per-year columns.

How each occurrence was scored

  • Entry = the last daily close before the event (events at or after 17:00 ET count from the next session; panchang day-rules from that day's open).
  • Windows of 3 days or more (a planet in a nakshatra or sign, Sun contacts…) are scored from entry to the last close inside the window, clipped to the backtest period. Instants and short windows (new moon, darshan, rise/set, ingress, vedha starts) are scored on the 5-trading-day move; 1-, 3- and 10-day moves are shown as a sensitivity check.
  • Moves under ±0.5% are FLAT. Rules whose verdict is Mixed or Neutral (both vedha kinds at once; the Indian festival-demand dates) are listed but not scored.
  • Hit rate = worked ÷ (worked + failed); flat occurrences are left out of both.
  • Base rate = the hit rate a rule would get by chance: among all windows of the same length in the same backtest year that moved more than 0.5%, the share that moved the rule's way. Over the whole period a 5-day window that moved went up 54% of the time, so a bullish rule needs to beat 54% and a bearish rule 46% to show any edge. Using each year's own base rate means a bullish rule gets no credit just for firing in a rising year.
  • Rule verdict: Worked = hit rate at least 10 points above its base rate and the average move went the stated way; Failed = at least 10 points below and the average move went the wrong way; otherwise Mixed. p-value = the chance of doing at least this well by luck at the base rate (one-sided binomial); green if below 0.05, red if the rule did significantly worse than chance. The per-year columns show worked/decided in each Nov–Nov year (5-year blocks in runs longer than 6 years), so a rule that only worked in one period stands out.

Do the rules add up? Net signal each day vs the next move

Each trading day: (number of distinct bullish silver rules active) − (number of distinct bearish silver rules active), with instants counted as active for one week; the combined Sun model is left out so nothing is counted twice. Correlation of that net count with the next day's return: -0.012; with the next 5 days: -0.024 (0 = no relation, positive = the rules pointed the right way).
